result.title: Neural Operator Splitting for Fluid Dynamics in Complex Geometry
result.summary: Solving dynamical systems in complex and diverse geometries remains challenging for both numerical solvers and learning-based surrogate models. We propose Neural Operator Splitting, a framework for learning fluid dynamics while preserving the physical structure of fractional-step numerical schemes. Instead of learning the full-step evolution monolithically, we decompose each time step into physically interpretable steps, and learn each operator separately using intermediate states from the underlying numerical solver. Guided by the linearity properties of the fractional steps, we introduce a conditional-linear Fourier neural operator (CL-FNO) whose linear state mappings are modulated by nonlinear conditioning on inputs such as boundary geometry. We further introduce two complementary strategies, symmetry sampling and corrective cycling, to mitigate error accumulation during autoregressive rollout. Experiments on 2D and 3D fluid flows with varying geometries and initial conditions show that our full model reduces mean relative $L^2$ rollout error by 68\% in 2D and 40\% in 3D compared with a single full-step neural operator. At comparable error levels, neural-operator inference is approximately $10^3$ times faster per step than the Monte Carlo solver.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Neural Operator Splitting，把流体单步演化拆成可物理解释的子步，并用数值求解器的中间状态分别训练各算子，配合条件线性傅里叶算子（CL-FNO）、对称采样与纠正循环来抑制自回归 rollout 的误差累积。
AI.relevance_reason: 用中间状态分步监督、以非线性条件调制线性状态映射、并显式处理多步 rollout 漂移，可能为 LVR 的分步 latent 更新监督、视觉条件状态转移与长程误差控制提供方法线索，需核查其可迁移性。
